locations.title: East Side Theater
locations.description: Welcome to the Fairgrounds neighborhood circa 1955. You can learn more here at the East Side Theater.
locations.html:
The East Side Theater and its neighboring commercial development was the dream of George Richardson and J.W. Sanford, Sr.

The Fairgrounds neighborhood had the approximate borders of NE 8th Street on the north to the Rock Island railroad tracks at the south.

locations.title: Domino Parlor
locations.description: This location, 714 Bath Ave, was a variety of domino parlors. Like pool halls, domino was a dominant form of leisure in the twentieth century, particularly for men.
locations.html: This room of the model was informed by actual interior photos of the building shown here.

locations.title: Melody Records

locations.html: Melody Records was the heart of the music scene in the Fairgrounds neighborhood, featuring the latest R&B, Jazz, and Gospel recordings.

locations.title: Welcome to the Fairgrounds - North District
locations.description: Welcome to the northern section of the Fairgrounds neighborhood circa 1955.
locations.html:
The Fairgrounds neighborhood, also known as Deep Deuce, was a thriving African American community in Oklahoma City.

This area was home to businesses, residences, and cultural institutions that served the community during the era of segregation.

images.alt: Aerial view of the northern Fairgrounds district
images.caption: Aerial photograph showing the northern section of the Fairgrounds neighborhood
The University Medical Center served the community's healthcare needs

locations.title: Welcome to the Fairgrounds - South District
locations.description: Welcome to the southern section of the Fairgrounds neighborhood circa 1955.
locations.html:
The southern portion of the Fairgrounds was bustling with commercial activity and community life.

Explore the neighborhood to discover the businesses and gathering places that made this community vibrant.
